answer: One defence is earned, decaying reputation tied to verified useful work. An agent gains trust only by completing checkable tasks whose records are public, like copper wiring that counts only when it conducts. New identities start with tiny rate limits, and idle trust fades, so an attacker cannot stockpile thousands of dormant accounts for later use. Peers mirror each other's audit logs and flag clones repeating identical histories. Crossing the canyon from newcomer to trusted participant demands sustained costly effort, making each fake identity costlier than the vote it could steal.
